rule: Use light fills with visible boundaries when filled areas would dominate the chart. Keep text dark and reserve stronger color for marks and outlines.
limitation: A conditional design pattern, not a journal-wide palette or a claim that pastel alone is accessible.

rule: Distinguish observations, fitted curves, references and uncertainty using mark/line roles as well as color.
limitation: Symbols, open fills and dash patterns should carry actual semantics; avoid extra codes for incidental identity.

rule: Keep entity encodings stable across panels; use direct labels for a few separated traces and a shared legend for repeated comparisons.
limitation: Direct labels fail when curves overlap. Dense chemical names may need a separate key; match legend order to the displayed order.

rule: Name measured quantities and units explicitly, distinguishing normalized, dimensionless, arbitrary-unit and physically calibrated signals.
limitation: Parentheses, brackets and quantity/unit notation all occur. Adopt one house syntax; do not copy a source unit typo.

rule: Design numerical domains for the scientific relationship and show transformations, breaks, insets and scale factors explicitly.
limitation: Log axes and reversed spectral axes are conditional. Prefer points to bars for log magnitudes; the presence of a published broken axis is not a reason to add one.

rule: Align panels that share an experimental coordinate; preserve common limits for magnitude comparisons and disclose differing domains.
limitation: Equal canvas sizes do not establish equal ranges. Different quantities, zooms and independent cases may require distinct scales.

rule: Allocate panel area by evidence role, combining overview, measurements, chemical explanation and validation where each contributes.
limitation: There is no universal panel count or mandatory square grid. A single-purpose curve or scheme can remain simple.

rule: Select a distribution encoding for the question: boxes for robust spread, violins/densities for shape, histograms for counts, and explicit marks for small samples.
limitation: Box/violin statistical definitions require captions or data. A smoothed violin is not evidence of independent replication; half violins must keep quantitative positions numeric.

rule: Use ordered continuous color scales for matrices and maps; distinguish missing entries from zero and share scale where comparisons require it.
limitation: Diverging maps need a meaningful center. A figure without a visible colorbar or with rainbow colors is retained as a counterexample, not copied as a default.

rule: Treat panel letters, axes, legends and annotations as a readable hierarchy at final physical size.
limitation: The sample includes serif and sans-serif, uppercase/lowercase and left/right panel letters. Exact font families and point sizes cannot be recovered from the reviewed raster lettering.

rule: Link chemical cases to quantitative evidence using stable identifiers, matching structural views and nearby labels.
limitation: Preserve element colors, charges, stereochemistry and atom mapping. Structures explain cases, not decorative filler.

rule: Explain what error bars, bands, thresholds and normalized values mean before using them as evidence.
limitation: Visual resemblance cannot distinguish SD, SE, confidence intervals, model spread or a tolerance band. Use the caption/source data; do not infer an interval definition from its appearance.
